lines.japanese: 「いってきまーす」
lines.english: “I'm off!”

lines.japanese: 朝、出かけに返事のない出発コールをする。今日もお向かいの魚眼レンズが僕を見送ってくれるはずだ。
lines.english: That morning, as I left, I called out my usual unanswered farewell. The fisheye lens across the street would see me off again today.
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: とと。そうだ、妹に伝えなくちゃいけないことがあったんだ。外の世界に踏みだしてすぐ、ドアノブを握ったまま足を止めた。
lines.english: Wait. That was right. There was something I needed to tell my sister. Barely one step into the outside world, I stopped with my hand still on the doorknob.

lines.japanese: 「小鳩ー、ちょっといいかな」
lines.english: “Kobato—have you got a minute?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: ふすまが開いて、朝食の後片付けをしていた彼女がひょこっと顔だけ出した。せっかく出ていったのに、もう一度帰ってきた兄をどう思っただろう。
lines.english: The sliding door opened, and she poked out her head from where she had been clearing away breakfast. I wondered what she thought of a brother who had made his exit only to come straight back.

lines.japanese: 「おれ、今日の夕食は友達と食べてくるから」
lines.english: “I’m having dinner with a friend tonight.”

lines.japanese: 毎日の家事をしてくれている妹には伝えておかないと。せっかく作ってくれた夕食が無駄になったら大変だ。
lines.english: I had to let my sister know, since she did the housework every day. It'd be awful if the dinner she made went to waste.

lines.japanese: 「え？　えっ？　よく分からなかった。も、もう一度、いいですか」
lines.english: “What? What? I didn’t understand. C-could you say that again?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。家には帰ってくるけど、そのあとまた出かけるから、おれの分の夕食は用意しなくていいよ」
lines.english: “I’ll come home first, but then I’m going out again, so you don’t need to make dinner for me.”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ」
lines.english: “What?!”

lines.japanese: 彼女は居間から廊下へと踏みだした。
lines.english: She stepped out of the living room and into the hall.

lines.japanese: そんな大ごとかな。たしかに、僕が友達と外食なんてしたのは……あれ、いつぶりだろう。
lines.english: Was it really that big a deal? Sure, the last time I ate out with a friend was... huh. How long ago was it?

lines.japanese: そんなことを考えている間に、小鳩は体を出すどころか玄関へと向かってきた。
lines.english: While I tried to remember, Kobato not only came all the way out but walked toward me at the door.

lines.japanese: 「あ、いいよ。そんな大したことでもないし。その、留守番ひとりにしちゃって悪いんだけど」
lines.english: “Oh, you don’t have to come all this way. It’s nothing important. I do feel bad about leaving you here alone, though.”

lines.japanese: 「あ……いえ、それはいい」
lines.english: “Oh... No, that's fine.”

lines.japanese: ふるふるふる
lines.english: Shake, shake, shake.

lines.japanese: 小鳩はいつもより大きく首を横に振った。動きが止まると、顔を上げて僕の目の位置にしっかりと視線を定める。
lines.english: Kobato shook her head harder than usual. Once she stopped, she raised her face and looked me straight in the eye.

lines.japanese: 「い、いってらっしゃい」
lines.english: “H-have a good day.”

lines.japanese: 「いってきます」
lines.english: “I'm off.”

lines.japanese: 小さく手を振る彼女の姿が、徐々にドアの隙間に埋められていく。ぱたんとドアを閉じると、カチリと鍵をかける音が内側から聞こえた。
lines.english: Her small wave was gradually swallowed by the narrowing gap of the door. It closed with a soft clap, and from inside came the click of the lock.

lines.japanese: 僕が自分で鍵をかけずに出かけたのはいつだったかな。そんなことを考えていたら、お向かいの魚眼レンズと目を合わせるのを忘れていた。
lines.english: When was the last time I'd gone out without locking the door myself? While I was thinking about that, I forgot to look the fisheye lens across the street in the eye.

lines.japanese: １２月の朝の通学路。まだ本格的な寒さにはなってないものの、１１月に比べると遥かに気温は低い。
lines.english: A December morning on the road to school. The real cold had yet to arrive, but the temperature was far lower than in November.

lines.japanese: 最近は秋がめっきり短くなった。そのせいで、ちょっと前までジャケットも脱いでたのに、すぐにコートを羽織る羽目になった。
lines.english: Fall had gotten awfully short lately. Not long ago I was going around without a jacket, and now I already had to throw on a coat.

lines.japanese: ただどんなに寒くても、１１月はやっぱり冬じゃないと思う。１２月になると途端に白くなる空は、冬の情景の中でも僕の一番好きな部分だ。まあ、錯覚だとは思ってる。
lines.english: However cold it got, I could never quite think of November as winter. The sky turning suddenly white with December was my favorite part of the winter landscape. I knew it was probably an illusion.

lines.japanese: だから、ぼうっと空を見上げながら歩いていたら、危うくかけられた声を聞き逃すところだった。
lines.english: So I was spacing out and looking up at the sky as I walked, and I almost missed someone calling to me.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君！」
lines.english: “Haneda!”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 声のした方に振りむいて見れば、煙草屋さんの小さな窓口に、ここ何日か見かけなかった人影があった。
lines.english: I turned toward the voice. There was someone at the tobacco shop's little window I hadn't seen for the past few days.

lines.japanese: 「ふふっ」
lines.english: “Hehe.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふふっ」
lines.english: “Hehehe.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふふふふっ」
lines.english: “Hehehehehe!”

lines.japanese: 窓口の奥で、僕に手招きしながら山科さんが笑ってる。
lines.english: Beyond the window, Yamashina laughed and beckoned me closer.

lines.japanese: 「おはよう」
lines.english: “Good morning.”

lines.japanese: 「あれ、山科さん。調子はいいの？」
lines.english: “Oh, Yamashina. Are you feeling better?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、調子～？　なんでなんで調子がいいかってどういうこと？　アガってんのかサガってんのか見て分かんないのか分かんないよねそうだよね、羽田君はどう調子？」
lines.english: “What, feeling? Better? What does ‘feeling better’ even mean? Up or down—can't you tell by looking? No, of course you can't, how could you? How are you feeling, Haneda?”
“What...?”

lines.japanese: あれ。なんだか、ていうか明らかに、いつもと様子が違うな。山科さんはものすごく機嫌がいいみたいだ。身を乗りだして、まくしたてるように喋りだした。
lines.english: Wait. Something about her was different. Very different. Yamashina appeared to be in a spectacular mood. She leaned through the window and launched into a torrent of words.

lines.japanese: 「うん、おれの調子はまあまあかな。山科さんは楽しそうだね」
lines.english: “I’m doing all right, I suppose. You seem cheerful today.”

lines.japanese: 「当ったり前じゃん、天気見てわかんないの、ピーカンだよ日本晴れだよ天晴れ天晴れ天気だよ。もう気分的にも西高東低で冬の気圧配置ど真ん中だよね、じゃあ羽田君もいっしょに、ハイ天晴れー！」
lines.english: “Of course! Can't you see the weather? Not a cloud in the sky—clear as clear can be, glorious, glorious, glorious weather! I'm high to the west and low to the east, a classic winter pressure pattern right down the middle! Come on, Haneda, you too—ready? Glorious!”

lines.japanese: 「はは、あっぱれー」
lines.english: “Haha. Glo-ri-ous!”

lines.japanese: 山科さんが楽しそうに両手を振りあげたので、僕もそれに倣うことにした。楽しいことはいいことだ。
lines.english: Yamashina happily threw both hands in the air, so I did the same. Fun was good.

lines.japanese: 「そんでそんで羽田君はなにしてんの、制服なんか着てどこ行くの八十日間世界一周？　はたまた宇宙？」
lines.english: “So so what are you doing, Haneda, where are you going dressed in that uniform? *Around the World in Eighty Days*? Or maybe outer space?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、今から学校なんだ」
lines.english: “I'm going to school.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ毎日が文化祭？　うっそ、すなわちエヴリデイ・イズ・フェスティボー？」
lines.english: “What, a school festival every day? No way, you mean every day is festiva-a-al?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、普通に学校だよ。山科さんは今日、体調いいみたいだね。良かった。実は卒文制作の手伝いをお願いしたくて――」
lines.english: “No, just ordinary school. You seem to be feeling well today, Yamashina. I’m glad. Actually, I wanted to ask if you could help with the graduation anthology—”

lines.japanese: 「やだな見てわかんない？　体調とかそーゆーんじゃないよ、見えないの私の漲るオーラ！　ちょっと待ってね頑張れば暖色系のうっすらしたもやみたいの見えるから、うーん、うーん、うう～……ん、見えた？」
lines.english: “Oh, come on, can't you tell? I'm not talking about my health or anything—can't you see this aura surging out of me? Wait, if I really try, you'll see this faint warm-colored haze, so... hnnn, hnnn, hnnnnn... See it?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。良かった、じゃあ今日は学校に来られそうなんだ。それなら卒業制作の――」
lines.english: “Yeah. Great, so it looks like you can make it to school today. Then the graduation—”

lines.japanese: 「えー、今日はって何もう酷いなあ、行くよ行くよ毎日行くよ。だけどうん、今日はちょっとお医者さん行かないといけないからお休みするけど、でもその気になれば病院が終わってからマッハで馳せ参じるよ」
lines.english: “What do you mean, ‘today’? That's so mean! I go, I go, I go every day! Okay, I do have to see the doctor today, so I'm taking the day off, but if I felt like it I could finish at the hospital and come galloping over at Mach speed!”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、それじゃ駄目だよ。病院に行くなら、今日は無理しないで休んだ方がいいよ」
lines.english: “No, you shouldn't. If you're going to the hospital, you should rest today instead of pushing yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「えーっ！　それもしかして私の心配してるの？　やだ、どうしよう、私ひとに心配なんてされるの生まれて初めてかもしんない。私、羽田君の友情を生涯忘れないから超ありがと、ほんとありがと」
lines.english: “What! Are you worried about me? Oh no what do I do, this might be the first time anyone’s ever worried about me! I’ll never forget your friendship as long as I live, Haneda. Thank you so much, really, thank you!”

lines.japanese: なんか……なんていうか、すごいな、今日の山科さん……。
lines.english: Somehow... How could I put it? Yamashina was extraordinary today...

lines.japanese: ひょっとして、これが彼女の言ってた波ってやつなのかな。上がる方の。
lines.english: Could this be what she meant by a wave? An upward one.

lines.japanese: 「そうだ、もし時間があるならお話しようよ、友情深めようよ、私いま誰かが通りかからないか待ちかまえてたの、そしたら羽田君とか歩いてるでしょ、もう笑いが止まんなくてそんな自分にまた噴飯ものだよね」
lines.english: “Oh, right, if you have time, let's talk, let's deepen our friendship! I was lying in wait for somebody to come by, and then who should come walking along but you, Haneda? I couldn't stop laughing, and then I had to laugh at how ridiculous that made me, right?”

lines.japanese: 「時間……なら、まだ間にあうかな。平気だよ」
lines.english: “Time...? I think I can still make it. That’s fine.”

lines.japanese: 「え、ホント？　やだ、じゃあ何の話しよー、時間ないなら簡潔に済ませた方がいいよね、短い方がいいよね、スペクタクルの部分だけ話した方がいいよね、私の人生全てがスペクタクルだけどその方がいいよね」
lines.english: “Really? Oh no, then what do we talk about—if you don't have time I should keep it short, right, shorter's better, only tell the spectacular part, right, although my entire life is spectacular, but that's still better, right?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、余裕はそんなにあるわけじゃないかな」
lines.english: “I don’t have that much time to spare.”

lines.japanese: 「だよね！　私もそうだと思ったからいま思いついたよ、羽田君のために考えたよ、ここ最近の一番のエピソード、昨日の夜に私に天啓が下りてきた話！　もうね、神が降りてきてね、明らかに神でね、わたし神かも！」
lines.english: “Right?! I thought so too, so I just picked one, I picked it for you, Haneda! The best story from lately: how a divine revelation came to me last night! See, God came down, definitely God, and maybe I'm God!”

lines.japanese: 「なんかねなんかね、近所に神社あるでしょ？　もうアレとか私のために建てられた感あるよね。どの辺が神かって言うと、あ、神社って言ったけど、欧米教的な神だからね、あ、話逸れたから戻すね」
lines.english: “So, so, there's that shrine nearby, right? It totally feels like it was built for me now. As for what part of me is God—oh, I said shrine, but I mean a Western-religion kind of God, okay, got sidetracked, back to it.”

lines.japanese: 「で、私の人生スペクタクルだからね、羽田君にどの部分が一番分かりやすく笑ってもらえるか考えたのね」
lines.english: “So my life's a whole spectacle, right? I was trying to figure out which part would get the biggest, easiest laugh out of you.”

lines.japanese: 「あれ、そのくだりは終わって、昨日の夜に神が降りてきたんじゃなかったっけ」
lines.english: “Wait. Wasn’t that part over? I thought God descended upon you last night.”

lines.japanese: 「やだ、そこ聞きたい！？　羽田君すごい、どうして私が話そうとしてたところ分かったの？　そう、昨日の夜に作詞してたら神降りてきたの。昨日、ひとと話してたらどんどんアガってきてね、もう天地創造だよ」
lines.english: “Oh you want to hear that!? Incredible, Haneda! How did you know exactly what I was trying to talk about? Yes, God came down while I was writing lyrics last night. I was talking to someone and getting higher and higher and then—creation of heaven and earth!”

lines.japanese: 「もう私の中で過去一番の大作と言ってもよくてね、あっ！　でも二番目？　それとも三？　でも三はないか……うん、二番目！　二番目にいい出来なんだけど、聞きたい？　どうする、今なら見せてもいいかも！」
lines.english: “It might be the greatest masterpiece of my entire life. Oh! No, second? Or third? No, not third... Yes, second! It’s the second-best thing I’ve ever made. Want to hear it? What do you think? I might show you right now!”

lines.japanese: 「いま？　ああ、ごめん、見せてもらいたいけど、ちょっといまは時間──」
lines.english: “Right now? Oh, I’m sorry. I’d like to see it, but I’m a little short on time—”

lines.japanese: 「見たい！？　やっぱ見たいよね、そうだよね！　見たいひといっぱいいるだろうけど、羽田君なら歴史的瞬間に立ちあわせてあげる。パソコンに入ってるから、ちょっと中入ってこられる？」
lines.english: “You wanna see?! Of course you wanna see, right, thought so! Tons of people probably want to, but since it's you, Haneda, I'll let you be there for this historic moment. It's on my computer, so can you come inside for a sec?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、朝からお邪魔するのは悪いし、ちょっといまは時間──」
lines.english: “I shouldn’t intrude this early, and I really don’t have time—”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあパソコン持って来るから待ってて！　デスクトップだけど、そこからでも見えるよね、いいでしょ見るくらいならなんとかなるでしょ」
lines.english: “Then I’ll bring the computer! Wait there! It’s a desktop, but you’ll be able to see it from out there, right? Sure you can. We can manage that much.”

lines.japanese: 「え、パソコンごと持ってくるの？　はは、いいよ次の機会に見せてくれればいいよ。そんな、わざわざ運んできてもらったら悪いよ」
lines.english: “You’re bringing the whole computer? Haha, no. You can show me next time. I’d feel terrible making you carry it all the way out here.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、そんなことないよ！　だっていま見た方がいいと思うよ、次きた時にはもう見らんないかもしれないよ、せっかく羽田君が見たいって言ってくれるなら、あ……やっぱり持ってくる」
lines.english: “What? No! I think you should see it now. It might be gone next time you come. If you’re kind enough to want to see it, then... Oh. I’m bringing it after all.”
“What...?”

lines.japanese: 唖然とする僕を置いて、山科さんは奥へと入ってしまった。まさか本気……じゃないよね。パソコンでしょ？　冗談だよね？
lines.english: Leaving me dumbfounded, Yamashina vanished into the back. She could not be serious... could she? A computer? She had to be joking.

lines.japanese: ていうか、時間そんなにないんだけどな……。
lines.english: Thing is, I really didn't have much time...

lines.japanese: 「ね、羽田君！」
lines.english: “Haneda!”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ、早いね」
lines.english: “Oh. That was fast.”

lines.japanese: １分で戻ってきた。やっぱり冗談だったみたいだ。
lines.english: She returned within a minute. Apparently it had been a joke after all.

lines.japanese: 「そういえばさっきまで、タロット占いしてたの忘れてたんだ。ねねね見てコレ見てコレ！」
lines.english: “I just remembered I was reading tarot cards until a minute ago! Look, look, look at this, look at this!”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、タロッ……ト？　パソコンで作詞じゃなかったの？」
lines.english: “Tar... ot? Weren’t you writing lyrics on the computer?”

lines.japanese: 「それがね聞いて、私さっきタロット占いしてたの忘れてた！　誰も占ったことないけど、当たるって評判だからね私の占い。とりあえずここから見て、見て見てコレ、このカードねＤＥＡＴＨって言うんだけどね」
lines.english: “Listen, I forgot I’d been reading tarot cards! I’ve never read for anyone, but my readings are famous for being accurate. Look from there, look look at this, this card is called DEATH.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、タロット占いはおれも少しだけ分かるよ。でもごめん、いまはちょっと時間が……」
lines.english: “Oh, I know a little about tarot myself. But I’m sorry, I don’t have much time...”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、興味あるの！　じゃあじゃあ占ってあげよっか？　私詳しいよ、チョー当たるよ、１００％に近い的中率誇るよ。羽田君なら無条件で占ってあげてもいいよ何がいい？　金運・恋愛運・はたまた寿命？」
lines.english: “You’re interested! Then shall I read for you? I know all about it. I’m crazy accurate, nearly one hundred percent! For you, Haneda, I’ll do it with no strings attached. What do you want—money, romance, or perhaps your life expectancy?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、うん、じゃあ……テストの結果とかがいいかな……」
lines.english: “All right, then... Maybe my exam results...?”

lines.japanese: 「えっえっ、テストの結果よくないの？　羽田君成績よかったよね、なのに悪いの、もしかしてテストのとき体調悪かった？　今月運気最悪なの？　大凶・仏滅・三隣亡？」
lines.english: “What what, your exams went badly? Your grades were good, weren't they, but you did badly? Were you sick during the exams? Is your luck terrible this month? Worst fortune, ill-starred days, doom for the neighbors?”

lines.japanese: 「どうなんだろ……それを占ってもらえばいいのかな」
lines.english: “I don’t know... Isn’t that what you’re supposed to find out?”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、運気が悪いならいいものあるよ！　タロット占いが好きなら、こういうのも興味あると思うんだ。ほんとすぐだから待ってて」
lines.english: “Oh, if your luck is bad, I have the perfect thing! If you like tarot, you’ll be interested in this too. It’ll only take a second, so wait there!”
“What? Wait—”

lines.japanese: 止める間もなく山科さんは奥へと入っていった。どうしよう、いつもなら電車に乗っている時間だ。
lines.english: Before I could stop her, Yamashina went into the back. What now? This was when I was usually on the train.

lines.japanese: 「ただいま！」
lines.english: “I'm back!”

lines.japanese: 「は、早いね……今度はなに、宝石？　山科さん、そんな高価なもの持ってるんだ」
lines.english: “Th-that was fast... What is it this time? Jewelry? I didn’t know you owned anything so expensive.”

lines.japanese: 「やだ、違う！　これね、この子たちね、パワーストーンって言ってね、癒し効果があったり色んな予防になったり水晶が守ってくれたりするの聞いたことない？」
lines.english: “No, silly! These little ones are called healing stones. Haven’t you heard that they can heal you and prevent all kinds of things and that crystals protect you?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、あるよ。一時期はやったりしたもんね」
lines.english: “Oh, yes. They were fashionable for a while.”

lines.japanese: 「でっしょ、もー羽田君分かってるねイケメン！　ほらほら翡翠とかトルマリンとか、見てるだけで力が沸いてくるよねそんな気するよね、このね、光沢感と石ならではのエッジが可愛くて仕方ないでしょ？」
lines.english: “Exactly! You get it, Haneda, you handsome devil! Look, jade and tourmaline. Just seeing them makes strength well up inside you, doesn’t it, you feel it too, right? That luster, those adorable sharp little edges only stones can have—aren’t they irresistible?”

lines.japanese: 「うんうん」
lines.english: “Yes, yes.”

lines.japanese: 「お気に入りの子には、この子ね、名前はガーネットのエレンで、こっちがラピスラズリのマリク。それとアメジストの男の子はジョルジュっていうの、もー可愛くて惚れ惚れしちゃうよね、親馬鹿だけどどう？」
lines.english: “These are my favorites. This one is Ellen the Garnet, and this is Malik the Lapis Lazuli. The amethyst boy is Georges. They’re so adorable I could stare forever. I know I’m a doting mother, but what do you think?”

lines.japanese: 「綺麗なんだね、見せてもらってもいいかな……あ、でも時間……」
lines.english: “They’re beautiful. May I see them? Oh, but the time...”

lines.japanese: 「なに時間って！　学校行く時間？　間に合わないのなんでなんで？　こんなとこで無駄なお喋りしてちゃ駄目じゃんヤダもー超ウケる、あ、じゃあ帰りにひとりでパワーストーンのお店に行ってみなよ」
lines.english: “What about the time? Time for school? You’re going to be late? Why why? You can’t stand around here wasting time chatting! Oh no, that’s hilarious. Then go to a healing-stone shop by yourself on the way home.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、じゃあ今度教えてもらおうかな」
lines.english: “All right. Maybe you can tell me where one is next time.”

lines.japanese: 「メモ用紙かなにか書くものない？　今から地図書いてあげるから行ってきなよ、きょ……明日にでも！　ね、じゃあ地図だけいま書いてあげるから」
lines.english: “Don’t you have a scrap of paper or anything to write on? I’ll draw you a map now, so go tod—tomorrow! Yes, I’ll just draw the map now.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、ごめん、だからもう時間が……」
lines.english: “No, I'm sorry, but as I said, I don't have time...”

lines.japanese: 「あ、手元にメモ用紙あった。じゃあ書くね地図、モンキホーテからの地図書くね、すぐ書くからちょっと待っててね」
lines.english: “Oh, I have paper right here. I'll draw it—a map from Monki Hote. It'll only take a second, so wait there.”

lines.japanese: その日僕は久しぶりに遅刻をして、恩田先生に怒られた。
lines.english: That day I was late for the first time in ages, and Ms. Onda scolded me.
